chapters.title: Job's Prosperity and First Test
chapters.synopsis: Job is described as a perfect and upright man, blessed with great family and wealth. In the heavenly council Satan challenges the sincerity of Job's faith, and with the Lord's permission strikes his flocks and children, yet Job worships and does not sin.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Job's character, family, and prosperity described

segments.speaker: satan
segments.note: Satan challenges Job's integrity before the Lord

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Messengers report Job's flocks and children destroyed

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job worships: the Lord gave and hath taken away

chapters.title: Satan Afflicts Job's Body
chapters.synopsis: Satan again appears before the Lord and is given power over Job's flesh, striking him with painful boils from head to foot. Job's wife urges him to curse God and die, but he refuses, and his three friends arrive to mourn with him.

segments.speaker: satan
segments.note: Satan is given power over Job's body

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Job is smitten with painful boils

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Job's wife urges him to curse God and die

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Three friends come to mourn with Job

chapters.title: Job Curses His Birth Day
chapters.synopsis: Breaking his silence, Job curses the day he was born and wishes he had died at birth rather than face such suffering. He longs for the quiet rest of death, where the weary find peace.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job curses the day of his birth

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job asks why he did not die at birth

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job longs for the rest of death

chapters.title: Eliphaz's Gentle First Rebuke
chapters.synopsis: Eliphaz gently chides Job for losing patience under his own trial after having strengthened so many others. He recounts a night vision teaching that no mortal can be more just or pure than God.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz gently rebukes Job's despair

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz recounts a night vision of God's holiness

chapters.title: Eliphaz Urges Job to Seek God
chapters.synopsis: Eliphaz continues that affliction springs from man's own doing, not from chance, and that the fool's anger destroys him. He urges Job to seek God, who wounds and also heals, and promises restoration to the one He corrects.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz says affliction springs from man's own way

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz urges Job to seek God's correction

chapters.title: Job's Grief Outweighs the Sea
chapters.synopsis: Job answers that his grief and calamity are heavier than the sand of the seas, which is why his words have been rash. He rebukes his friends for failing him like a brook that dries up when needed most.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job's grief outweighs the sand of the seas

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job rebukes his friends as a failing brook

chapters.title: Job Asks Why God Watches Him
chapters.synopsis: Job laments that life is a hard service, brief and full of misery, with no hope of return once it ends. He turns and asks God directly why He watches and tests every mortal so closely.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job laments the brevity and misery of life

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job asks God why He watches him so closely

chapters.title: Bildad Defends God's Justice
chapters.synopsis: Bildad argues that God never perverts justice, and that Job's children must have sinned to deserve their fate. He urges Job to seek God early, promising that the pure and upright are never truly forsaken.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Bildad the Shuhite argues God is always just

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Bildad urges Job to seek God and be restored

chapters.title: Job Longs for a Daysman
chapters.synopsis: Job marvels at God's incomparable power over the mountains, the sea, and the stars, admitting no mortal could contend with Him. He laments that there is no umpire to lay a hand upon them both and mediate his case.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job marvels at God's incomparable might

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job wishes for a daysman between him and God

chapters.title: Job's Complaint to His Maker
chapters.synopsis: Weary of his life, Job pours out his complaint before God, asking why He formed him so carefully in the womb only to let him suffer now. He pleads for a little ease before he goes to the darkness of death.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job pours out his complaint asking why he was made

chapters.title: Zophar Calls Job to Repent
chapters.synopsis: Zophar rebukes Job sharply for defending himself and insists that God's wisdom is far beyond human understanding. He urges Job to put away his iniquity, promising that his life would then shine brighter than noonday.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Zophar the Naamathite rebukes Job's self-defense

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Zophar promises peace if Job puts away sin

chapters.title: Job Mocks His Friends' Wisdom
chapters.synopsis: Job answers sarcastically that wisdom will not die with his friends, for even he understands as much as they do. He turns to describe God's sovereign power over nature, kings, nations, and counselors.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job mocks his friends' claim to wisdom

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job recounts God's sovereign power over all things

chapters.title: Job Pleads His Case Before God
chapters.synopsis: Job accuses his friends of forging lies to defend God and declares he would rather reason his case directly before the Almighty. He begs God to withdraw His terror and reveal to him what sins he has committed.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job accuses his friends of speaking falsely for God

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job asks God to show him his transgressions

chapters.title: Job Reflects on Man's Brief Life
chapters.synopsis: Job reflects that man born of woman is of few days and full of trouble, cut down like a flower. He wonders aloud whether a man, once dead, might somehow live again, and half hopes for such a renewal.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job reflects on man's brief life and the hope of renewal

chapters.title: Eliphaz Warns of the Wicked's Fate
chapters.synopsis: Eliphaz accuses Job of undermining reverence for God with vain and windy words. He then describes at length the terror, darkness, and ruin that overtake the wicked man.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz accuses Job of undermining reverence for God

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz describes the wicked man's terrible fate

chapters.title: Miserable Comforters and a Heavenly Witness
chapters.synopsis: Job calls his friends miserable comforters who add to his sorrow instead of easing it, and describes how God's hand seems set against him. Yet he appeals to a witness in heaven who can vouch for his innocence.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job calls his friends miserable comforters

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job appeals to a witness for him in heaven

chapters.title: Job's Hope Turns to Dust
chapters.synopsis: Job feels mocked on every side and his spirit broken, his days extinguished like a fading lamp. He tells his friends that if he has any hope left, it lies only in the grave.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job feels near death and mocked by all

chapters.title: Bildad Describes the Wicked's Doom
chapters.synopsis: Offended that Job counts his friends as beasts, Bildad describes at length the snares, terrors, and desolation that await the wicked man. His light is put out, and his memory perishes from the earth.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Bildad describes the doom of the wicked

chapters.title: I Know My Redeemer Liveth
chapters.synopsis: Job pleads with his friends to have pity on him, for God's hand alone has wrought his misery and left him abandoned by all he loves. Yet in the depth of his suffering he declares his certain faith that his redeemer liveth and will stand at the latter day upon the earth.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job pleads with his friends for pity

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job declares, I know that my redeemer liveth

chapters.title: Zophar on the Wicked's Brief Joy
chapters.synopsis: Zophar answers that the triumphing of the wicked is short and their joy but for a moment. He describes how the riches such men swallow will be vomited up again and how the wrath of God overtakes them.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Zophar describes the wicked's brief triumph and fall

chapters.title: Job Observes the Wicked Prosper
chapters.synopsis: Job challenges his friends' tidy theology by observing that the wicked often live long, grow mighty, and die in peace and honor. He asks why, if God truly punishes sin at once, such men so often prosper unpunished.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job observes that the wicked often prosper

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job challenges his friends' simple theology

chapters.title: Eliphaz Accuses Job of Sin
chapters.synopsis: Eliphaz now accuses Job directly of specific sins, such as withholding bread from the hungry and oppressing the fatherless. He urges Job to acquaint himself with God and be at peace, promising that light will then shine upon his ways.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz accuses Job of specific hidden sins

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Eliphaz urges Job to acquaint himself with God

chapters.title: Job Longs to Find God
chapters.synopsis: Job longs to come before God's seat and lay his case in order, confident he could reason with Him. Though he cannot find God in any direction he searches, he trusts that when God has tried him, he will come forth as gold.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job longs to find God and plead his case

chapters.title: Job Describes the Oppressed and Wicked
chapters.synopsis: Job describes the plight of the poor, fatherless, and oppressed who suffer at the hands of the wicked while God seems to delay judgment. He wonders openly why the Almighty does not set clear times of reckoning.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job describes the oppressed and the wicked's impunity

chapters.title: Bildad: No Man Is Pure
chapters.synopsis: In a brief final word, Bildad affirms that dominion and fear belong to God, whose armies are without number. He asks how a man born of woman could ever be pure, since even the stars are not clean in God's sight.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Bildad briefly affirms no man is pure before God

chapters.title: Job Extols God's Majestic Power
chapters.synopsis: Job answers Bildad with biting sarcasm, asking how such counsel has truly helped one so weak. He then extols God's majestic power, who stretches out the north over empty space and hangs the earth upon nothing.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job answers Bildad's speech with sarcasm

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job extols God's majestic power over creation

chapters.title: Job Vows to Keep His Integrity
chapters.synopsis: Job solemnly swears that as long as breath remains in him, his lips will not speak wickedness and he will not let go his integrity. He then describes the miserable portion appointed to the wicked man, as his friends have claimed.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job vows to maintain his integrity till death

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job describes the portion of the wicked man

chapters.title: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found
chapters.synopsis: Job muses that men can mine silver, gold, and precious stones from the earth, yet true wisdom cannot be found in the land of the living or bought at any price. Only God knows its place, for the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job muses that wisdom is harder to find than gems

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Only God knows wisdom's place: fear of the Lord is wisdom

chapters.title: Job Recalls His Honored Days
chapters.synopsis: Job recalls the days when God's candle shone upon his head and he was honored as a father to the poor and a champion of the fatherless. He remembers being heeded by princes and elders alike as one whose words brought comfort.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job recalls his former days of honor and prosperity

chapters.title: Job's Present Disgrace and Pain
chapters.synopsis: Job contrasts his former honor with his present disgrace, now mocked even by the outcasts of society. His body is racked with pain night and day, and he cries out to God without receiving any answer.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job describes his present affliction and disgrace

chapters.title: Job's Oath of Innocence
chapters.synopsis: Job swears a solemn oath that he has kept himself from lust, falsehood, deceit, and oppression of the poor. Point by point he invites judgment upon himself if any of these charges could be proven true, closing his defense.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job swears he has kept from lust, falsehood, and deceit

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job's closing oath of innocence ends his defense

chapters.title: Elihu Rises in Anger
chapters.synopsis: The three friends fall silent since Job will not yield, and a younger man named Elihu grows angry, both at Job for justifying himself and at the friends for failing to answer him. He explains why, though young, he feels compelled to speak.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu the younger grows angry at all four men

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu explains why he must now speak

chapters.title: Elihu Speaks of God's Ransom
chapters.synopsis: Elihu tells Job that God speaks to men through dreams, visions, and the chastening of pain to turn them from pride. He describes how, if a messenger is found, God may grant a ransom and deliver the man from the pit.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu says God speaks through dreams, pain, and a ransom

chapters.title: Elihu Defends God's Justice
chapters.synopsis: Elihu argues before Job and his friends that it is impossible for God, the Almighty, to do wickedness or pervert judgment. He insists that God renders to every man according to his ways, whether prince or pauper.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu defends the absolute justice of God

chapters.title: Elihu on Man and God
chapters.synopsis: Elihu asks Job what profit his righteousness brings to God, since man's sin or virtue affects his fellow man far more than the Almighty. He suggests that Job's cries have gone unanswered partly because they arose from pride rather than humble trust.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu argues man's conduct does not diminish God

chapters.title: Elihu on Affliction's Purpose
chapters.synopsis: Elihu teaches that God uses affliction to open men's ears to instruction and turn them from iniquity. He then marvels at God's greatness displayed in the gathering of waters and the power of the thunderstorm.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu says God teaches through affliction

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu marvels at God's power in the storm

chapters.title: Elihu Marvels at the Storm
chapters.synopsis: Elihu continues describing the wonders of thunder, lightning, snow, and wind, all obeying God's command across the earth. He concludes that men cannot fully order their speech before such glory, and that God is excellent in power and justice.

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: Elihu describes God's wonders in the storm and sky

chapters.title: The Lord Answers from the Whirlwind
chapters.synopsis: The Lord answers Job out of a whirlwind, demanding to know where Job was when the foundations of the earth were laid. Question after question about the sea, the stars, the snow, and the light overwhelms Job's understanding of creation's mysteries.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord questions Job out of the whirlwind

chapters.title: The Lord Questions Job on Creatures
chapters.synopsis: The Lord continues, describing His care for the wild goat, the untamed wild ass, the ostrich, the war horse, and the soaring eagle. Each creature displays a wisdom and freedom that Job could never have given them himself.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord describes His care for the wild creatures

chapters.title: Job Humbled; Behemoth Described
chapters.synopsis: The Lord challenges Job to answer if he still dares to contend with the Almighty, and Job humbly admits he has nothing to say. The Lord then describes the great beast behemoth, whose strength is beyond any man's control.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord challenges Job to answer Him

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job humbly admits he has no answer

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord describes the great beast behemoth

chapters.title: The Lord Describes Leviathan
chapters.synopsis: The Lord describes leviathan, a fearsome sea creature that no man can capture, tame, or make a servant. Its scales, breath, and strength picture a power that belongs to God alone to master.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The Lord describes the mighty leviathan

chapters.title: Job Repents and Is Restored
chapters.synopsis: Job repents in dust and ashes, confessing that he had spoken of things too wonderful for him to understand. The Lord rebukes Job's three friends and accepts Job's prayer on their behalf, then restores Job's fortunes twofold, giving him a new family and long life.

segments.speaker: job
segments.note: Job repents in dust and ashes

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: The Lord rebukes the friends and accepts Job's prayer

segments.speaker: chronicler
segments.note: The Lord restores Job's fortunes twofold
